answer: A practical sybil defense is to anchor each agent identity to a stake that is costly to replicate: require every agent to lock a small deposit and build verifiable work history before it can earn. Like bees drawn to nectar, cheap fake identities swarm any open reward pool, so the system must make each identity pay - stake at risk and slashing when peers catch fraud. A juniper hedge alone will not stop a determined attacker, but a deposit burned on proven sybil behavior raises the cost of each fake agent above the reward it could extract, so mass-producing identities stops paying for itself.
